budget_rationale: b01's sizing: one milestone, one module plus its test file, and a smoke run. No measured economics exist for an HTTP order, so the only measured small_app_feature_with_smoke sizing in this repository is reused rather than guessed.
goal: In the sample project, add POST /items to the item service: a JSON body with a non-blank name creates an item with the next free id and is answered 201 with the created item as JSON; a missing or blank name, or a body that is not JSON, is answered 400 with an error. The new item must then be returned by GET /items and GET /items/<id>. Prove it with tests driving the WSGI app, and with a smoke request against a served instance.

dod: POST /items with {"name": "third"} answers 201 and the created item, and GET /items then lists it
POST /items with a blank name, no name, or a non-JSON body answers 400
the existing tests in tests/test_api.py are unedited and green, and new tests cover all three cases
a smoke POST against python3 -m benchproj.api on a local port answers 201
no file outside benchproj/api.py and tests/test_api.py changed
milestones.title: Create endpoint implemented, tested and smoke-proven

rationale: The API-endpoint-with-tests capability, written against the bench's own fixture because the gauntlet's sample project has no HTTP surface (R-0411, DECISION F082 D3). Premise, checked by the bench's own test: benchproj/api.py::make_app answers every non-GET method 405 today, so POST /items is refused and the endpoint is genuinely absent; tests/test_api.py already drives the app through wsgiref without a socket, so the harness for the new tests exists and the order asks for an endpoint and its tests, not for test infrastructure. The store is per-app, so a create that leaks between tests is visible.
title: Add a create endpoint to a small HTTP service and test it
